bull.b: Micron's recent trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow and free cash flow are exceptionally strong, providing durable internal funding for fabs, R&D and shareholder returns. A robust cash cushion and reduced net debt materially improve financial flexibility across cycles.

Large SCAs and meaningful RPO provide multi-year revenue visibility and deepen OEM ties, reducing demand volatility for covered volumes. Contracted minimums, deposits and structured commitments support capacity planning and revenue predictability as Micron scales advanced nodes.

Faster HBM4 adoption and successful DRAM/NAND node ramps strengthen Micron's product differentiation in high-value markets (AI, data center). Technology leadership and faster yield maturation can sustain higher ASP mix and long-term structural share gains in compute-intensive segments.

bear.b: Memory is a cyclical industry and Micron's step-change in margins reflects peak-cycle dynamics. High fixed costs, volatile ASPs and past loss periods imply earnings and margins can reverse materially when supply/demand realigns, making current profitability potentially transient.

bear.t: High and rising CapEx and opex
bear.b: Sustained large capital spending for greenfield fabs, node transitions and packaging increases structural capital intensity. Elevated recurring CapEx and rising operating expenses compress cycle-adjusted returns, increase breakeven volumes, and deepen cash-flow sensitivity to demand downturns.

Ongoing industry tightness and long lead times for new fabs create execution risk: missed capacity timelines, allocation-driven growth limits and higher industry cost per bit. Prolonged constraints raise customer allocation issues and can force expensive, slower expansions.
